Produce.note: v8 per-record errors (KIP-467), v9 flexible, v10 leader hints (KIP-951), v11 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890), v12 transaction-version-2 implicit add-partitions (KIP-890 part 2), v13 topic IDs (KIP-516, Kafka 4.1; may return UNKNOWN_TOPIC_ID).

Fetch.note: v11 rack / preferred read replica (KIP-392), now fully handled: OFFSET_NOT_AVAILABLE (78) skips the partition for one round and keeps the follower, and an OFFSET_OUT_OF_RANGE from a follower drops the preferred replica and re-resolves against the leader. v12 flexible + LastFetchedEpoch (sent at its -1 default; truncation is detected through OffsetForLeaderEpoch instead), v13 topic IDs replace names (KIP-516; a request whose topics are not all known by id is capped at v12), v14 OFFSET_MOVED_TO_TIERED_STORAGE (KIP-405), v15 ReplicaState (KIP-903), v16 leader hints (KIP-951), v17 ReplicaDirectoryId (KIP-853), v18 HighWatermark (KIP-1166). Fetch sessions (KIP-227) are not implemented: every fetch is a full fetch (sessionId 0, sessionEpoch -1).

ListOffsets.note: v4 leader epoch (KIP-320), v6 flexible, v7 max-timestamp (KIP-734), v8 earliest-local offset (KIP-405), v9 last-tiered offset (KIP-1005). v10 (async remote list offsets, KIP-1075) and v11 (earliest pending upload offset, KIP-1023) are deliberate gaps, not a waiver: both are tiered-storage features this client does not use.

Metadata.note: v7 leader epoch (KIP-320), v9 flexible, v10+ topic IDs, v13 adds a top-level error code and is where REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED surfaces (KIP-1102).

OffsetCommit.note: v6 committed leader epoch (KIP-320), v7 group instance id, v8 flexible, v9 member epoch (KIP-848), v10 topic IDs.

OffsetFetch.note: v5 leader epoch, v6 flexible, v7 require-stable (KIP-447), v8 multi-group batching, v9 member epoch (KIP-848), v10 topic IDs. The fork has no v0 codec, which is correct: v0 read offsets from ZooKeeper.

FindCoordinator.note: v3 flexible, v4 multi-key batch (KIP-699), v5 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890), v6 KeyType SHARE=2 (KIP-932, broker-internal). apiKeys.js still calls key 10 GroupCoordinator, the pre-0.11 name.

JoinGroup.note: v5 encodes groupInstanceId but nothing plumbs it: Broker.joinGroup() has no such parameter, so static membership (KIP-345) is inert today.

LeaveGroup.note: v3 batch removal by group instance id (KIP-345): the codec exists, but there is no admin removeMembersFromConsumerGroup to drive it.

DescribeGroups.note: v3 IncludeAuthorizedOperations/AuthorizedOperations (KIP-430), v4 member GroupInstanceId (KIP-345), v5 flexible, v6 per-group ErrorMessage and GROUP_ID_NOT_FOUND for a group that does not exist (KIP-1043). Below v6 a broker reports a KIP-848 consumer-protocol group as Dead, so describing one also needs ConsumerGroupDescribe (key 69) routing.

ListGroups.note: v3 flexible, v4 StatesFilter/GroupState (KIP-518), v5 TypesFilter/GroupType (KIP-848). Java's downgrade rule applies to the filters on older brokers: a state filter needs v4, and a type filter needs v5 unless it asks only for classic (and consumer), which a broker without group types answers identically unfiltered.

SaslHandshake.note: Never flexible, and the only API in the matrix that is fully current.

ApiVersions.note: v0-v3 omit every SupportedFeatures entry whose MinVersion is 0 (KAFKA-17011, fixed in v4 / Kafka 3.9), so a v3-only client sees a truncated feature list. The flexible-protocol pilot targets v4 and falls back to v3 only for brokers below 3.9.

CreateTopics.note: v5 flexible, v7 returns topic IDs.

DeleteTopics.note: v6 can delete by topic ID; the fork sends each topic name with the zero uuid, as the Java client does when it is given names.

InitProducerId.note: v2 flexible, v3 re-initialization with the producer's current id and epoch (KIP-360), v4 PRODUCER_FENCED, v5 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE, v6 two-phase commit (KIP-939) and latestVersionUnstable, so brokers advertise 0-5 by default.

AddPartitionsToTxn.note: v2 PRODUCER_FENCED, v3 flexible. v3 is the client ceiling: the message definition keeps v4 (batched transactions, VerifyOnly) and v5 for broker-to-broker calls, so behind:2 is this API's steady state. Under transaction version 2 (KIP-890 part 2) a client does not send it: Produce v12 adds the partition implicitly.

AddOffsetsToTxn.note: v2 PRODUCER_FENCED, v3 flexible, v4 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE (KIP-890). Under transaction version 2 (KIP-890 part 2) a client does not send it: TxnOffsetCommit v5 adds the offsets implicitly.

EndTxn.note: v2 PRODUCER_FENCED, v3 flexible, v4 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE, v5 returns the producer id and epoch the coordinator bumped to (KIP-890 part 2). A transaction stays at v4 or below unless its coordinator finalizes transaction.version at level 2 or above in ApiVersions v3+; v5 being advertised is not the signal.

TxnOffsetCommit.note: v2 committed leader epoch, v3 flexible with KIP-447 group metadata (generation, member id, group instance id), v4 TRANSACTION_ABORTABLE, v5 adds the offsets to the transaction itself under transaction version 2, so no AddOffsetsToTxn precedes it. A transaction stays at v4 or below unless its coordinator finalizes transaction.version at level 2 or above.

DescribeAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

CreateAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

DeleteAcls.note: v1 is the 4.x floor and is also the fork's maximum.

AlterConfigs.note: Replaces the resource's whole dynamic config: an entry left out is deleted. IncrementalAlterConfigs (key 44) changes only the entries it names.

AlterPartitionReassignments.note: One of the only two flexible-encoded codecs in the fork today: it hand-rolls the tag buffer inside the request body because the request header is still hardcoded to v1. It must migrate when real flexible header selection lands. v1 adds AllowReplicationFactorChange.

ListPartitionReassignments.note: The other hand-rolled flexible codec; same migration applies. Kafka defines only v0, so the fork is current by accident.

OffsetForLeaderEpoch.note: Leader-epoch fencing (KIP-320): v3 and v4 are implemented. v2 is a deliberate gap, not a waiver - versions below 3 require CLUSTER permission, which clients are not typically granted, and the Java consumer pins its own floor at v3 for that reason.

IncrementalAlterConfigs.note: The merge-semantics alternative to AlterConfigs: each config entry names a SET, DELETE, APPEND or SUBTRACT, so the entries a request leaves out are untouched.

ConsumerGroupHeartbeat.note: Required for the KIP-848 consumer group protocol (groupProtocol: 'consumer'), GA since Kafka 4.0.

ConsumerGroupDescribe.note: Admin-side counterpart of KIP-848; needed so group descriptions stop reporting consumer-protocol groups as Dead.

DescribeTopicPartitions.note: Admin describe at scale, and the only way to read eligible leader replicas. The API does not exist on brokers below 3.8, so the Metadata path must stay as a fallback; ELR arrays are null unless the cluster runs eligible.leader.replicas.version=1.

SaslAuthenticate.note: v1 adds SessionLifetimeMs (KIP-368 re-authentication), v2 is flexible. The mechanism-provider contract is unchanged at every version: a provider returns INT32-length-prefixed bytes from request.encode() and receives them in response.decode() - v2 strips and re-wraps that prefix inside its own codec.

crossCutting.gap: Topic IDs (UUIDs) are not yet used by every API that accepts them
crossCutting.where: offset-commit and offset-fetch paths, topic administration
crossCutting.impact: Cluster metadata caches each topic's id, and Fetch and Produce are keyed by it (falling back to names for a request whose ids are not all known). What remains: OffsetCommit v10 and OffsetFetch v10, KIP-848 assignments (phase-6), and topic ids on CreateTopics v7 / DeleteTopics v6 (phase-8).

Every fetch is a full request - sessionId 0, sessionEpoch -1, an empty forgotten-topics list - so a poll re-sends every assigned partition rather than only what changed. This is a decision, not an oversight: 3.0.0 ships sessionless (decision D31), and the three fetch-session error codes are mapped defensively so an unexpected one cannot crash a consumer. Incremental fetch is the prerequisite for reducing request size on a large assignment.
Unreachable against a 4.x broker, which never negotiates Produce below v3 or Fetch below v4. The decoders must stay: old segments can still be returned inside a modern Fetch response.

UNKNOWN.reason: KafkaJS has exposed this name as KafkaJSProtocolError.type since 1.x; renaming it is a breaking public-API change.

NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 2.6 (KIP-392); the KafkaJS name is public API.

GROUP_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11 when coordinators stopped being group-only; the KafkaJS name is public API.

GROUP_COORDINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11; the KafkaJS name is public API.

NOT_COORDINATOR_FOR_GROUP.reason: Kafka renamed the constant in 0.11; the KafkaJS name is public API.
